text:
Evidence supports specific diagnostic-to-action mappings, rather than a general claim that fault detection predicts intervention gains. [Dataset Cartography](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.746.pdf) uses training confidence/variability to select data, then retrains and evaluates generalization. [Koh and Liang](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/koh17a.html) evaluate influence-guided label repair against random and loss-based inspection. These are intervention experiments, but do not establish calibrated selection among arbitrary architecture, optimizer, or sampling changes. Mutation-fault accuracy alone therefore cannot validate that selection policy.

Policy-learning research supplies a stronger framework: estimate action-specific incremental value, then evaluate the learned policy separately. [Athey and Wager](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02896) use cross-fitted doubly robust scores; their causal guarantees require identification and overlap assumptions. [High Confidence Policy Improvement](https://psthomas.com/papers/Thomas2015b.pdf) separates candidate selection from safety evaluation. [Policy Learning with Abstention](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=ppWhBLJNbD) formalizes deferral under uncertainty. Applied here: freeze diagnostics before intervention, calibrate against actual subsequent validation gains, separate policy fitting/tuning from evaluation by entire task or trajectory, and retain the baseline when evidence is insufficient. These are design implications, not existing validation for RecHarness.

For four routes, use a prospectively randomized guidance placebo with matched compute, action availability, recommendation frequencies, and stopping rules. Shuffle diagnostic-to-action assignments while retaining repeated recommendations and temporal dependence as blocks; independently shuffling every recommendation creates false replication. [Winkler et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4010955/) explain exchangeability restrictions. Four distinct route bundles permit only 24 permutations; repeated actions can reduce distinct assignments further. Identical recommendations make shuffling uninformative. Report realized action changes and paired gains, and treat nonrandom route shuffles as sensitivity analyses unless exchangeability is justified.
